lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to a brand-new world. Last time, we found a map with a green leaf in the Amber Library. We opened the back door of the library, and look! We are in a big glass house full of plants. This is the Green Laboratory. A laboratory is a place for experiments. Many people say lab for short. Scientists study plants here. Say it with me. Scientists study plants here. Great job! Here comes the head scientist. He's a very old tortoise, and his name is Dr. Moss. He moves slowly, but he thinks fast. There's a sign on the wall. Let's read it. "Welcome to the Green Laboratory. Here, we ask questions about nature. We look closely, we measure carefully, and we write down everything. Please do not touch the Sleeping Seed." Hmm, the Sleeping Seed? What's that? Dr. Moss says, It's a very old seed. It never opened. Maybe you can help me someday. Now, phonics. Microscope. Microphone. Microwave. Microchip. Micro means small. A microscope helps us see small things. Let's start our science adventure!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Before we do any experiments, we need to learn the lab rules. Safety first! Dr. Moss is holding a pair of goggles. Goggles protect your eyes. Wear your goggles. Don't touch the hot plate. Say it with me. Wear your goggles. Don't touch the hot plate. Very good! When we tell someone a safety rule, we start with a verb. Wear. Don't touch. Wash. And we can say need to. We need to wash our hands after the experiment. Let's read the safety poster together. "Lab Safety Rules. One: Always ask an adult first. Two: Wear your goggles. Three: Don't touch the hot plate. Four: Never taste anything in the lab. Five: Wash your hands after the experiment. Six: If something spills, tell an adult right away." Great reading! Rule number four is very important. Some things look like juice, but they are not juice! Now, phonics. Telescope. Periscope. Kaleidoscope. Stethoscope. Scope means a tool for looking. A telescope helps us look at faraway stars. Let's be safe scientists!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will use a real microscope. Dr. Moss puts a tiny piece of a leaf on a glass slide. Now, look through the microscope. Turn the knob slowly. What can you see? I can see tiny circles! Say it with me. I can see tiny circles! Wonderful! To say more, use looks like. It looks like a green honeycomb. These tiny circles are the parts of the leaf. We call them cells. Every plant has many, many cells. Let's read Dr. Moss's note about the microscope. "This microscope makes things look one hundred times bigger. A leaf looks flat and smooth to your eyes. But under the microscope, you can see many small green boxes and circles. Plants are full of tiny surprises!" Isn't that amazing? Remember, use small sentences. I can see. It looks like. It's green. Now, phonics. Thermometer. Speedometer. Pedometer. Barometer. Meter means a tool for measuring. A thermometer measures how hot or cold something is. Next time, we will use one! Let's look closely like real scientists!

Now, read the number. The water is 20 degrees. Say it with me. The water is 20 degrees. Good! Next, the ruler. How long is this leaf? It's 15 centimeters long. When you measure, start at zero, and hold the ruler straight. Scientists always check. Let's measure it again to check. Here is a page from Dr. Moss's measuring notebook. Let's read it. "Monday morning. The water in the fish tank was 20 degrees. The big leaf was 15 centimeters long. The small leaf was 6 centimeters long. Monday afternoon. The water was 23 degrees. The sun made it warmer." So, the morning and the afternoon were different. Numbers help us see changes. Now, phonics. Microscope. Telescope. Thermometer. Thermostat. Thermo means heat. Meter means a tool for measuring. Put them together, and you get thermometer! Let's measure everything!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Every scientist has a lab notebook. Today, we will learn how to write one. Dr. Moss writes in his notebook every day. A good page has four parts. The date. What I did. What I saw. And a picture. Here's a new word. Observe. Observe means to look very carefully. Today, I observed a leaf. Say it with me. Today, I observed a leaf. Excellent! Let's read Haru's notebook page. "Date: May 12. Today, I observed a leaf. I used a microscope and a ruler. The leaf was 15 centimeters long. Under the microscope, I saw tiny green circles. They looked like a honeycomb. Question: Why are leaves green?" Wow, Haru even wrote a question. Scientists always have new questions. Use past tense in your notebook, because you write after the experiment. I used. I saw. It was. Now, phonics review. Microphone. Periscope. Pedometer. Thermometer. Small, look, measure, heat. Now, write your first notebook page. Write four or five sentences, and draw a picture. Let's be careful observers!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will do our first experiment. Before an experiment, a scientist makes a guess. That's called a prediction. Predict means to say what will happen. Here's a big tank of water. Here's an apple. Will it float or sink? I predict the apple will float. Say it with me. I predict the apple will float. Wonderful! Now, ask your friend. What do you predict? You can also say I think. I think the stone will sink. Let's read the experiment card from Dr. Moss. "Float or Sink? You need: a tank of water, an apple, a stone, a coin, a leaf, a carrot and a plastic spoon. Step one: Hold each thing over the water. Step two: Write your prediction. Step three: Put it in the water gently. Step four: Write the result." Remember, a prediction is not right or wrong. It's just a smart guess. Scientists are happy when they are surprised! lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will write a lab report. A lab report has four parts. Purpose. Prediction. Result. Conclusion. Our report has four parts: purpose, prediction, result and conclusion. Say it with me. Our report has four parts: purpose, prediction, result and conclusion. Great! The purpose is why we did the experiment. The conclusion (けつろん) is what we learned. Let's read Riko's lab report. "Purpose: The purpose of our experiment was to find out about plants and music. Prediction: We predicted the music plant would grow taller. Result: After two weeks, the music plant was 14 centimeters tall. The quiet plant was 13 centimeters tall. Conclusion: The music plant grew a little more. But one centimeter is a very small difference. We only used two plants. We can't be sure yet. We need to try again with more plants." What an honest report! Good scientists don't jump to a big answer. They say, We can't be sure yet. Now, phonics review. Telescope. Equipment. Photography. Shiny. Observation. Let's write our lab reports!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is our goodbye tour of the Green Laboratory. Let's remember everything. In the safety room, we learned the rules. Wear your goggles. In the water room, we said, I predict the apple will float. The egg floated! If you heat ice, it melts. In the storeroom, we said, It's made of wood. Paper is made from trees. And in the greenhouse, we said, Plants need sunlight to grow. We learned a lot in the Green Laboratory. Say it with me. We learned a lot in the Green Laboratory. Beautiful! Oh, wait! Kiko found a very old notebook in the storeroom. It belonged to Dr. Moss's grandfather. Let's read the last page. "I found the Sleeping Seed on a snowy mountain. Seeds from cold places are clever. They wait for winter. If the seed feels a long, cold winter, it knows that spring is coming. Then it can wake up." A cold winter! Seeds from cold places need cold first. Dr. Moss puts the seed in the fridge for a winter. Now, phonics review. Thermostat. Environment. Magnetic. Muddy. Migration. Let's finish our goodbye tour!
